_comment: Prototype: X/Twitter restricted form. Only 'this NAMED tweet URL exists with this text on this day' via X's official public oEmbed endpoint. Open-ended 'did @acct post anything' and any NO-by-absence are NOT resolvable in v1 (see vault note).
claim: The tweet at https://x.com/jack/status/20 exists, is authored by @jack, contains the text 'just setting up my twttr', and carries a posting day between 2006-03-21 and 2006-03-22 (exclusive).

elements.q: Does the X oEmbed response for the named tweet URL show author @jack, the text 'just setting up my twttr', and a displayed posting date on 2006-03-21?

custom_definitions: Deadline and window bounds are UTC instants pinned in the time block; 'UTC_V1' applies and no local time zone is ever read.
Early resolution: YES may be declared at the first qualifying post; NO may be declared only at/after the deadline and only with the coverage proof below.
Burden of proof is on YES: a post that is not shown in an admitted exhibit, or an ambiguous one, resolves NO, never YES by default.

Fallback: if the live fetch is unavailable or blocked, a keeper snapshot taken inside the window may be used; if neither is available the resolver reports COULDNT_CHECK and retries on the recovery ladder before VOID; a blocked or rate-limited page is never evidence of absence.
oEmbed exposes only a calendar date (no time of day), so window bounds are day-aligned UTC midnights and the displayed date is read as that UTC day.

The tweet is identified by its numeric status id; the handle in the URL is cosmetic. A 404/410 from oEmbed cannot distinguish deleted, private, suspended or never-existed, so it is COULDNT_CHECK and never NO.
Only the named tweet qualifies; the bet cannot be YES because some other tweet matches, and it cannot be NO because no other tweet was found.
